Configuration

Widgetry reads its settings from a single object passed when the library starts. Every option has a default, so an empty object is a valid configuration, and you add keys only where you want something different.

Where settings come from

Three layers are merged each time the library starts. The built-in defaults come first; then a file named widgetry.json in the working directory, if there is one; and finally the object you pass in code. A later layer wins for any key it sets and leaves the rest untouched.

Merging is shallow for scalar options and recursive for the theme and events sections, so overriding one colour does not discard the others. Arrays are replaced whole, never concatenated.

Note. The configuration file is read once, at startup. Changing it later has no effect until the library restarts.

A minimal example

var app = Widgetry.Start(new Options
{
    Theme = "dark",
    Locale = "en-GB",
    MaxItems = 200,
});

This starts the library with the dark theme and British English formatting, and limits lists to two hundred items. Everything else keeps its default.

Options

Theme
Name of a registered theme. Defaults to "light". An unknown name is an error at startup, not a silent fallback.
Locale
A language tag used for number and date formatting. Defaults to the host's current setting.
MaxItems
The largest number of items any list will hold. Values below 1 are treated as 1. The default is 1000.
Timeout
Seconds to wait for a slow component before giving up. Zero means wait forever, which is rarely what you want.

Environment overrides

Any option can be set from the environment by prefixing its name with WIDGETRY_ and writing it in upper case. Environment values sit between the file and the code in precedence, which makes them convenient for deployments.
